--------
In this VladTV interview, Rex Holloway explains the turning point that led him to walk away from the Aryan Brotherhood at age 22. From Texas prison units like Torres, Ferguson, and East Ham, Holloway describes growing disillusioned with prison politics, weak leadership, and the reality of life in solitary confinement. He recalls reading about John Gotti, Paul Castellano, and Sammy “The Bull” Gravano’s *Underboss*, which changed how he viewed loyalty and trust in organized crime.

The conversation centers on a botched prison hit involving poison-laced tacos, a written kite, and a chain of mistakes involving Wizard, Dirty Joe, and a man nicknamed Iceman. As the conspiracy unraveled, Holloway says he realized he could spend life in prison over “sloppy” decisions and chose to quit before the fallout hit. A rare firsthand look at gang life, prison hierarchy, and leaving extremism behind.

Charleston White sits down with Vlad to react to the latest controversy surrounding NBA Ben10, the NBA YoungBoy associate who went from flaunting money, jewelry and street image online to facing jail while using a wheelchair. White questions claims reportedly made in a legal filing that Ben10 cannot use the bathroom on his own, arguing that the situation is being framed to help him get released from custody. He points to past videos of Ben10 riding in an electric chair, posing with weapons, and maintaining a tough persona as potential evidence prosecutors could use against him.

The conversation also touches on the sudden shift from “street” bravado to complaints about jail conditions, with White comparing it to his own brief stay in Brown County. Vlad and White discuss accountability, public image, social media evidence, and how legal strategy can shape narratives around incarceration.

--------
In this VladTV interview, former Mexican Mafia member Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza details the moment his undercover cooperation became public after Kern County homicide charges were reopened in 1978. Mendoza describes being placed in custody with figures including Joel Morgan, “Black Dan,” and Vital Rodriguez, hearing murder plans while preparing to testify in cases across Fresno, Hayward, Visalia, and Los Angeles. He recalls taking the stand against former associates, the pressure on his family, and being moved into protective housing before entering Witness Protection.

Mendoza also recounts a warning from U.S. Marshals in Buffalo, New York: authorities believed the Mexican Mafia had traded murder contracts with the Italian Mafia to target him. With Ronald Reagan in town delaying the marshals, Mendoza says he was told to pack lightly, meet at Batavia Downs, and was later flown to Philadelphia near Veterans Stadium while officials conducted a threat assessment.

Former Delta Force operator Dale Comstock joins Vlad to break down his early days in the elite unit, serving as a team breacher and preparing for his first major mission in Panama. Comstock discusses how U.S. forces viewed Manuel Noriega, the unelected Panamanian strongman accused of drug trafficking, intimidation, torture, and controlling the government through fear. He explains the months of training that led up to the operation, the threats facing Americans in Panama, and the strategic importance of the Panama Canal. The conversation also connects Noriega’s rule to broader discussions about dictatorships, Saddam Hussein, Iran, China’s influence, and U.S. military intervention. Comstock details the mindset behind entering dangerous targets first and the mission context surrounding the rescue of an American from a Panama prison with 120 shooters involved.
